_readme: THE RIG — what is actually on the other end of each MIDI channel.
The browser's contract is fixed: nine ROLES on nine channels, CC74 per
channel as that layer's energy, CC1/CC2 the raw hands, MIDI clock for
tempo. This file is the OTHER half of the contract: what instrument sits
on each channel in the Live set, how it sounds, and when a scene should
reach for it. It is design-time knowledge, not runtime — nothing in the
page reads it. It exists so a Claude session designing a scene's sound
can write for YOUR rack instead of an imaginary one, and so the three of
you agree on what channel 5 IS.
Fill in `instrument` (device/preset name as it appears in Live),
`character` (how it actually sounds — dark/glassy/plucky/breathy...),
and `use` (when a scene should want it). Honest beats aspirational:
describe the patch you have, not the one you plan.
Keep it current the cheap way: change the Live set → update this file in
the same breath, commit both. A Claude session can also scaffold this
file from the .als itself (it is gzipped XML — drop it in the repo and
ask), or eventually via an Ableton MCP link. Until then, hand-edited.
Per-track convention that makes CC74 work everywhere: each track is an
Instrument Rack whose MACRO 1 is mapped to the patch's brightness/cutoff,
and CC74 on that channel drives Macro 1. Swap the instrument inside the
rack freely — the mapping survives.
_channelMap: ASSUME RIGGED, MAP 1:1 (Lance's law, Aug 2026): the browser always sends FULL MIDI for every role — nothing is ever held back because a patch is missing. A silent console row = drop an instrument on that track. Channels map 1:1 to the Live set:
tracks left-to-right = ch 1-15, and it is PENCIL, not ink: we reshape it together
as the racking walk meets each scene. The rack serves the scenes and the art;
no assignment below is precious except where marked as Lance's own call:
1 R&B DRUMS=perc (renamed from TRANCE DRUMS, Aug 2026) · 2 80'S DRUMS (alt kit, unassigned) · 3 SYNTH BASS=bass ·
4 SFX=sfx · 5 PADS=pad (Jup-8 V4 Deep Blue Voices) · 6 STRINGS = Arturia Augmented Strings (RACKED & READY — bench; Event Horizon's gate target) ·
7 FELT PIANO=lead · 8 SHRINE (RACKED & READY — Sacred Shrine color, bench) · 9 HANDPAN=texture · 10 Mellotron (RACKED & READY, bench) ·
11 Choir (RACKED & READY — Vespers hum candidate) · 12 SpaceSax (RACKED & READY — Lumen/Vespers fallback color) · 13 Nebula=bed (racked) ·
14 ARP SYNTH=arp (Lance renamed the Omnisphere track; his rule: rhythmic, enters WITH drums, on grid) ·
15 BELLS=bells (Omnisphere KPRO Dreamies) · 16 MIDI (utility, ch16 — fixed).

CASTING BENCH: a racked track with no role gets cast PER SCENE in Live — set its MIDI From to the role channel the scene needs (e.g. Vespers: CHOIR listens on Ch. 5 for that scene). Two clicks, reversible; the 1:1 map stays the default.
The `ch` values below are BAKED as the browser's default map at build time
(part2c reads RIGDOC.roles[].ch) — edit here, rebuild, and every browser
matches the set. The RIG panel remap is a per-browser override on top.
CONFIDENCE (Lance, Aug 2026): drums, SFX one-shots, felt piano and Augmented
Strings are his calls; bass builds to the CHARACTER spec; every other seat is
provisional — designed to the briefs in docs/ABLETON-RIG.md, moved freely
whenever a scene asks. He is unattached; the scene decides.

BENCH ROLES (Aug 2026): strings 6 · shrine 8 · mellotron 10 · choir 11 · sax 12 — every racked track is now a role under the 1:1 law; scenes cast onto them directly (EH wall→strings, Vespers beam→sax + choir double, Ferro answers→mellotron). The MIDI-From casting-bench move is retired for these; it remains the trick for kit swaps (80'S DRUMS listening on ch1).
_cc74_mappings: THE MAPPING REGISTRY (facts only — update when a mapping is made or removed; sessions must NOT assume beyond this list):
ch1 perc: CC74 → LEX loop pad chain volume (Min -inf, Max 0dB)
ch4 sfx: CC74 → ThunderRain chain vol (-61..-9dB) + Rain chain vol (-22..-2.4dB) — the weather crossfade
ch7 lead: CC74 → FELT PIANO Auto Filter freq (20Hz..20kHz)
ALL OTHER CHANNELS: CC74 UNMAPPED — it does nothing in Live yet.

Worth mapping next (Lance, when ready): ch15 bells → Dreamies Master Filter cutoff (Omnisphere right-click → MIDI CC Learn → BELLS row MAP) · ch14 arp → Science Class cutoff (same trick) · ch5 pad → Jup-8 Brightness (Arturia exposes it as a host param: Live Configure) · ch9 texture → HandPan brightness/send.
When loops land on 54/55/56/57 (Chladni/Ridge/EH/Ferro loop seats): map ch1 CC74 to each pad's chain volume, Min -inf — same move as the LEX pad; one CC fades whichever loop its scene holds.
New lanes worth mapping: ch6 strings → Augmented Strings GATE dial (the marquee — EH streams gate depth here now) · ch12 sax → the beam patch's cutoff (Vespers streams THE MOUTH here now).

THE EXPRESSION ROUND (Lance wants it): map CC74 on every seat so scenes can swell/ramp instead of hitting - ch3 bass (Lumen's breath swell is already streaming it), ch5 pad, ch8 shrine, ch11 choir, ch12 sax, ch6 strings gate, ch10 mellotron. Each mapping ~2 min (Configure/CC-Learn + the row's MAP button); say each one as it lands and it gets recorded here.
DONE ch2 TRANCE DRUM: CC74 -> pad 56 chain volume Min -inf (Lance, Aug 2026)
DONE ch16 SYNTH CZV: CC74 -> filter cutoff. WANTED ch16 CC71 -> the ACID/FX macro (the SECOND LANE: MOut.expr2 streams CC71, parked at 0; EH drives it with motion + window energy)
_tracks_note: EXACT Live track names, left to right = ch 1-16 — the console rack and RIG panel print these so the browser reads like the Ableton mixer. Rename a track in Live → rename it here in the same breath.
clock: 24 PPQN from the page; enable Sync on the port, press EXT

lead.instrument: Splice felt piano — the John Legend one (FELT PIANO track, loaded)
lead.use: melodic triggers — plucks, tones, answers. Rain Atrium's felt piano lives here by design. Chladni sends no lead notes but streams resonance as CC74 — map to a brightness/send macro

pad.instrument: Ethereal Journey - an Augmented Strings patch (PADS ch5, Lance, Aug 2026 - swapped in over Jup-8 Deep Blue Voices: 'those were too gritty'). 1:1 rule: the pad ROLE plays the track NAMED PADS. RULE (Lance): the pad is INTENTIONAL - single placed notes, never a constant wash. MAPPING DIRECTION (Lance, Aug 2026): ch5 CC74 must point at a control where 127 = FULL body -- the engine parks every CC74 at 127 on scene open/close, and mapped to Morph that read 100% = thinnest; fix is Min/Max swapped in the Live MIDI map (Min 127, Max 0), never a scene-side workaround.
pad.character: the most scene-divergent channel — glass / cathedral air / analog light-pad / dark gated strings; chain per scene (manual first, bed-note chain-select later)
pad.use: sustained voice-led chords; glides on chord changes. Event Horizon (SRC-13) streams its rhythmic GATE DEPTH here as CC74 — map it to Augmented Strings' gate dial and the plugin throbs with the picture

bass.instrument: SYNTH BASS track, loaded — patch name TBD (say it in a session and it lands here). Design brief: Serum-style sine sub always on + CHARACTER macro: round (Ridge bans saw) → bite (White Study) → detuned-saw maw (Vespers' own spec)
bass.character: clean and fat at rest, teeth up the CHARACTER macro; sidechain-ducked by the perc kick (comp keyed to the R&B DRUMS ch1 group, LP 150Hz sidechain EQ) so the pump exists only when a groove is earned
bass.use: root movement; keep the sub for the wall (bass-mono below ~120Hz). Chladni's lock bass and beat-mode doubling land here; Ridge's funk figure and White Study's pump live mid-macro. Full recipe: docs/ABLETON-RIG.md

arp.instrument: ARP SYNTH (Lance's track 14, loaded — his Omnisphere rhythmic patch). RULE (Lance, Aug 2026): the ARP is RHYTHMIC — it enters WITH the drums, on the grid; never nature-timed, never under held notes
arp.character: arpeggiating synth; cutoff + resonance ARE the performance controls
arp.use: sequenced grid patterns only, gated by a scene's beat mode (Night Circuit, Chladni's unlock). CC74 → cutoff is this patch's native play. Vespers' churn arrives here as CC74 only

bells.instrument: Omnisphere — KPRO Dreamies (BELLS ch15) — Lance's verdict after playing: 'not really bells, more Canadian-boards pads' — a patch he loves but not a bell. SEAT OPEN: still wanted here = real bells + the deep TOLL (tam-tam, long tail). Until then Chladni rings its bells BROWSER-side (midi:false) — scene OUT=BOTH to hear them
bells.character: glass strikes for Lumen, chimes for Weather's heading bells, one enormous struck-metal toll for Chladni's lure — velocity sensitivity ON, NO internal rhythm (a groove patch here fights nature-timed strikes)
bells.use: chimes, sparkles, lock blooms, White Study's summon roll; Chladni's 1-in-7 lure toll goes to the TOLL chain — a real tam-tam, not a piano (docs/ABLETON-RIG.md Part 3)

texture.use: the continuous-voice mirror: held notes that re-strike on retune, CC74 = pooled voice energy. Chladni's mode tones: every detent catch is a mallet strike on a literal resonant plate

perc.instrument: THE R&B KIT (Lance's call, Aug 2026) — the loaded drum rack IS the R&B/lo-fi kit, built out per the pad map: 36 kick (round boom-bap thump + ghost layer) · 38 snare/side-stick · 39 clap/snap · 42 closed hat (dusty) · 43/45 toms lo/mid · 46 OPEN hat (dusty, medium decay) · 49 soft crash wash · 51 shaker · 53/F2 = Rain Atrium's LEX loop pad — and THE LOOP SEATS (Aug 2026, loop-first drums): 54/F#2 = Chladni's break loop · 55/G2 = Ridge's funk loop (~96 BPM) · 56/G#2 = Event Horizon's dark techno loop (128-feel) · 57/A2 = Ferro Bloom's dub loop (TL_LD_140_Drums_Dubbed, hip-hop dub, 140 source — Warp ON as 8 bars, Beats mode, so it follows the clock down to Ferro's 100) — each struck once at its window's first open and held, faded entirely by ch1 CC74. THE PARKING LAW (Aug 2026, learned live): BOTH drum tracks (R&B DRUMS and TRANCE DRUM, the second kit) listen on ch1, so a seat strike fires the pad in EVERY ch-1 rack -- pads 53-57 are LIVE SHOW SEATS in all of them, and a 'parked' loop candidate on any of those pads WILL play in the wrong scene (a dub loop parked on 54 played inside Chladni). Park candidates at C3/60 and up; only a chosen loop goes on its seat, in whichever rack. Seats: 53 Rain (LEX) / 54 Chladni (EMPTY by choice -- Lance keeps the programmed one-shot beat) / 55 Ridge / 56 EH / 57 Ferro (TL_LD_140 dub) (map each pad's chain volume Min -inf, the LEX move); empty pads are silent, programmed kits still play until a loop is seated. Original LEX note: 53/F2 = Rain Atrium's LEX loop pad (Simpler: Loop+Warp ON, Transpose 0, Vel→Vol 0, chain vol mapped to ch1 CC74 Min -inf) — deliberately OUTSIDE the kit zone so other scenes' kicks (note 36) never restart it. A SECOND kit (Fred Again / trance — hard kick tuned A, break slices, taiko top-velocity zone) gets built separately; how scenes pick kits = the chain/remap decision, deferred until it exists
perc.character: trance weight under Fred Again break character; group chain = EQ → Glue 2:1 slow attack → Drum Buss ~50% wet (Boom on A) → parallel comp ~25%; wash send 1.4s/predelay 14ms/low-cut 250Hz on 38/46 only. Per-pad vel→vol ~60% — the browser streams real velocity
perc.use: drum rack — 36 kick/low thud · 38 mid crack · 42 click · 46 air/tick; scene noise-hits arrive bucketed by brightness. The rail-secret break plays this kit. Swing comes from the SCENE, never Live (grooves don't apply to live MIDI). Full recipe: docs/ABLETON-RIG.md

sfx.instrument: SFX rack — LOADED (Lance, Aug 2026): C#1/37 = brooding lightning · D1/38 = quick loud strike · D#1/39 = forest rainfall loop (held all scene) · E1/40 = thunderstorm loop (held, crossfades in) — CC74 rides both loop chains' volumes (forest Min ~-22dB, storm Min ~-60dB). F1/41 = VESPERS' WAKE SEAT (the scene fires sfxNote(41) on the first touch after stillness -- wants a growly one-shot that BENDS UP into the hit: Simpler pitch env Amount -2st, Decay ~150ms, drive/saturation on; empty since the Aug 2026 rack rebuild, which is why the wake went silent in OUT=midi). Still to add: Blade Runner chops / cave drips one-shots, Granulator sand for Chladni
sfx.use: semantic one-shots — 36 ignition · 37 lightning · 38 thunder · 39 rain. Chladni streams sand motion as CC74 → density/volume. Event Horizon streams its swallow charge/rise as CC74 — map to a riser/impact send

bed.instrument: Nebula (ch13) — Lance's ear: 'sounds like you're on a spaceship cruising — has some bass and hum to it that's nice.' Exactly the bed. — LOOP ON REQUIRED (Aug 2026): the scene holds ONE note-on for the whole scene; an unlooped sample plays out and the bed dies mid-scene (Lance: "Nebula keeps turning off").
bed.use: one held note per scene = THE SCENE'S ROOT minus an octave, clamped to the hum band 24-43 (Aug 2026 — the old 20+SRC formula climbed to shrill keys on the pitched sampler; Lumen's bed was B-flat 3). Scene-atmosphere chain selection, if ever built, will use its own mechanism, not the bed pitch.

strings.instrument: Arturia Augmented Strings (STRINGS track ch6) — now a first-class ROLE: Event Horizon casts its string wall here (V18), gate depth streams on ch6 CC74 — map it to the Augmented gate dial (the marquee mapping's real home)
strings.character: dark low string ensemble with a rhythmic gate the CC74 stream drives
strings.use: EH's chairs + chord rolls; any scene wanting bowed weight

shrine.instrument: SHRINE (Sacred Shrine, ch8) — Lance's ear: 'a little more tone' than Nebula. Role reserved; the tonal-atmosphere wildcard (audition low before casting — his earlier verdict: 'really busy' as a lead pad).
shrine.character: tonal sacred atmosphere — more pitch than Nebula's hum
shrine.use: THE TEASE SEAT (Lance, Aug 2026): 'hit it for a second, just one note, and that's a 10-second tease.' Rest-state single notes ride the long tail - Lumen V24 breathes on it. Still audition low anywhere it plays under other material.

mellotron.instrument: Mellotron (ch10) — Lance: 'makes a fun lead, pretty high'. Ferro casts its call-and-response answers here (V21)
mellotron.use: high answering lines; audition against White Study's summon roll

choir.instrument: Choir (ch11) — Vespers holds a soft root+color double under the hum (V13), velocity breathing with the light
choir.use: hum doubles, walls at totality; keep the fader low — seasoning, not lead

sax.instrument: SpaceSax (ch12) — Lance's ear: 'a RECORDING of a sax playing a soulful note... never really play a run with it. A really high-quality SWELL on the mid-to-top end with nice texture.' It is a swell COLOR, not a melodic voice — pitch-tracking a recording across register chipmunks. For Vespers' beam, load a mono analog (Mini V, legato+glide) as a second chain on this track and use the sax swell where a held color is wanted.
sax.character: soulful sax swell recording — mid/top texture, one-note color
sax.use: SWELLS: a single held color that blooms (Lumen aperture peaks, Ferro sustained-lead hole). NOT runs, NOT the retuning beam - that needs the mono-analog chain beside it

drums2.instrument: TRANCE DRUM (second kit rack, moved from ch1 to ch2 Aug 2026 -- ends the shared-ch1 seat collisions). Its loop shelf: 56/G#2 = EVENT HORIZON's jam loop (DS_VS_100_drum_full_grace, pop/synthwave, 100 native -- warped, struck at the drop and held; map ch2 CC74 -> pad 56 chain volume Min -inf, the LEX move) . 59/B2 = EH's riser (VSH1_one_shot_fx_3_you_got_me, 8s, warped as 2 Bars -- the scene strikes it exactly 2 bars before the drop). Parking for candidates: C3/60 and up.

synth.instrument: CZ V (SYNTH CZV, ch16) — Vespers V15 runs it as THE ANNIHILATION ALIEN's voice (preset in use: Neurosis). Lance's two mapped controls ARE the expression lanes: PITCH BEND = the scoop (set CZ V bend range to 2 semitones; the scene parks bend at center on scene edges) and ch16 CC74 = the PANNER macro (the voice follows the figure's centroid across the field). ch16 CC71 streams the GROWL — map it to a Timbre/FX macro to bring the fold into the rack. Event Horizon (break versions, V29 and earlier) uses the same track with its self-patterning preset + CC74 filter / CC71 ACID — preset per set list until a two-chain rack exists.

_benchCasting: THE BENCH CASTING SHEET (per-scene, two clicks each, reversible — set the bench track's MIDI From to the role channel and its Monitor to In; undo after the scene). The 1:1 map stays the default; these are the doubles worth auditioning:

VESPERS (SRC-09): the BEAM off the felt piano — put a mono/legato analog voice (Omnisphere or Mini V: glide ON ~40ms, CC74 -> cutoff) on the SPACESAX track, MIDI From = Ch 7, and turn FELT PIANO's monitor off for this scene. The MOUTH stream (lead CC74) then articulates it as designed. CHOIR: MIDI From = Ch 5 at low volume — the hum grows a human undertone.

EVENT HORIZON (SRC-13): STRINGS (Augmented) MIDI From = Ch 5 — the chairs land on the instrument the gate mapping was designed for; keep PADS muted or layered under. CHOIR From = Ch 5 doubles the wall for totality.
LUMEN (SRC-38): audition glass on PADS first; SPACESAX From = Ch 5 is the fallback aperture color. SHRINE From = Ch 5 is the wildcard (busy — Lance's verdict — but organ-shaped; try at low volume).
FERRO (SRC-15): MELLOTRON From = Ch 7 — Lance: 'makes a fun lead, pretty high' — the call-and-response answers and birth rolls sit right in its range. Felt piano off or layered.
WHITE STUDY (SRC-34): MELLOTRON From = Ch 7 as the summon-roll color if the stab A/B lands elsewhere.
WEATHER (SRC-10): nothing benched — the seat that matters is real chimes on ch15.
Say what you cast in a session and it gets recorded here as the scene's standing cast.
